metadata.title: Karlovy Vary Day Trip from Prague — Private Car & Chauffeur
metadata.description: A private day trip from Prague to Karlovy Vary in a Mercedes with your own chauffeur: the colonnades and hot springs, an optional stop at Loket Castle, and the drive back the same day.
metadata.ogTitle: Private Day Trip from Prague to Karlovy Vary

hero.label: Private Day Trip · Karlovy Vary
hero.headlineItalic: The spa town, at your own pace.
hero.intro: A private day trip from Prague to Karlovy Vary: a Mercedes and a chauffeur collect you at your hotel, drive you west to the spa town, wait while you walk the colonnades and bring you back the same day. From €{dayKarlovyE} for the whole car, there and back.

items.label: Price
items.value: From €{dayKarlovyE} per car, there and back — not per person

items.label: Time there
items.value: Four to five hours for the colonnades and lunch

items.label: Included
items.value: Hotel pickup, chauffeur waiting on site, fuel and motorway tolls

paragraphs: Karlovy Vary — Carlsbad — is the largest spa town in the Czech Republic. Its hot springs rise under a line of colonnades along the river Teplá, and visitors still walk from one to the next with a porcelain cup, as they have since the days of Goethe and Beethoven.
The town is about 1 hour 45 minutes west of Prague, most of it on the D6 motorway. A day is enough to walk the colonnades, taste the springs, have lunch and see the Grandhotel Pupp.

A private car matters here for a practical reason: the spa centre is largely closed to traffic. A chauffeur who knows the town brings you as close to the colonnades as the rules allow, and waits there.

items.title: The colonnades and the springs
items.body: The Mill Colonnade, the Market Colonnade and the Hot Spring Colonnade with its geyser are within a short walk of each other. Drinking cups are sold at stalls along the way.

items.title: Grandhotel Pupp and the lookout
items.body: The hotel at the end of the promenade is worth a coffee. The funicular behind it climbs to the Diana lookout tower above the town.

items.title: Glass and Becherovka
items.body: The Moser glassworks and the Becherovka museum both take visitors. Check opening hours and tour times before you travel.

items.title: A stop at Loket Castle
items.body: Loket, a small castle town in a bend of the river Ohře, lies a few minutes off the route. Tell us when you book if you would like to stop and we confirm it in writing.

items.title: One price for the car
items.body: €{dayKarlovyE} in an E-Class (up to 3 passengers), €{dayKarlovyV} in a V-Class (up to 6) and €{dayKarlovyS} in an S-Class. The price is for the car, not per person, and covers the drive there, the wait and the drive back.

items.title: Child seats at no charge
items.body: Infant, toddler and booster seats are free. Tell us the children’s ages when you book and the right seats are fitted before pickup.

steps.label: How it works
steps.heading: Booking a day trip in four steps.

items.title: Book a return trip
items.body: In the booking form enter your Prague address and the destination, choose a return trip and set the return for the same day. A rough return time is enough — it can move on the day.

items.title: Choose the car
items.body: E-Class for up to three, V-Class for up to six with room to spare, S-Class for an executive day. You see the price for the whole car before you pay.

items.title: Meet your chauffeur
items.body: You receive the chauffeur’s name and phone number in advance. They collect you at your hotel or apartment door at the agreed time.

items.title: Take your time
items.body: The chauffeur waits near the centre while you visit. Call or message when you are ready and the car comes back for you.

editorial.label: Good to know
paragraphs: The spring water is warm and mineral, and most people sip rather than drink it. The colonnades are free to walk at any time of year.
During the Karlovy Vary International Film Festival in early July the town is very busy and traffic rules in the centre change. Book early for those dates and allow more time.

Your chauffeur is a professional driver, not a tour guide: they know the road, where to drop you and where to wait, but they do not lead tours. Entrance tickets, meals and guided tours are not part of the price. If you would like a licensed local guide, book one for the hours you plan to be there and we time the drive around it.

faqs.q: How much is a private day trip from Prague to Karlovy Vary?
faqs.a: €{dayKarlovyE} in an E-Class (up to 3 passengers), €{dayKarlovyV} in a V-Class (up to 6) and €{dayKarlovyS} in an S-Class. That is the price for the whole car for a daytime trip, there and back, with the chauffeur waiting while you visit. Fuel and motorway tolls are included. The exact fare for your date is shown in the booking form before you pay.

faqs.q: How long does the day trip take?
faqs.a: Plan about eight to nine hours in total: roughly 1 hour 45 minutes each way and four to five hours in Karlovy Vary. Leaving Prague at 9:00, you are back around 18:00.

faqs.q: Does the chauffeur wait and drive us back the same day?
faqs.a: Yes. That is what a day trip is: the same car and chauffeur take you there, wait near the centre and drive you back to your Prague address. You do not look for a taxi or a train for the return.

faqs.q: Is a guide or entrance ticket included?
faqs.a: No. The price covers the car and the chauffeur. Tickets and guided tours are booked separately, and the chauffeur does not act as a guide. We are glad to time the day around a guide or a ticket slot you have booked.

faqs.q: Can we stop at Loket Castle on the way?
faqs.a: Yes. Loket is a short detour from the route. Tell us when you book, and we confirm the plan and the price in writing before the trip.

faqs.q: How many people fit in one car?
faqs.a: Up to three passengers in an E-Class or S-Class and up to six in a V-Class. Larger groups travel in two or more cars. Child seats are free in every class.
